semantic_closure.statement: The constructions in \(\text{def:twoarm-sorting}\) equal \(J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(J_{nb}^{+}\) for \(K=2\). For each fixed \(K\), feeding the observable assigned-arm measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)}\) into the finite primal programs in \(\text{def:fixed-k-lp}\) attains \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\), and their Kantorovich duals have the same values. These are exact convexified empirical endpoints. At any single history node, every rational optimal plan is realized by a deterministic fixed-potential-outcome block completion after finite replication of that node's armwise lists, so its LP endpoints are asymptotically nodewise completion-attainable as block sizes grow. No same-size integrality assertion for \(K>2\), and no cross-history assertion that one \(\Xi_n\) realizes independently chosen nodewise plans, is made.
semantic_closure.justification: The result turns the abstract envelope into sorting for two arms and a finite auditable computation for multiple arms.
semantic_closure.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance gives two-arm rearrangement, while GaoGeQian2025MOT gives static MOT computation; neither states the finite-population replication boundary needed for adaptive design-based sharpness.
semantic_closure.consumer: A four-arm complete-block redesign of the NewbyEtAl2025MentalHealth minitrials can compute each endpoint using a fixed-\(K\) transportation program.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For \(K=2\) and \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), the identity
\[
\frac12(x-y)^2=\frac12x^2+\frac12y^2-xy
\tag{1}
\]
shows that the two marginal square terms do not depend on the coupling. The cited rearrangement result \(\mathrm{lem:twoarm\text{-}rearrangement\text{-}extrema}\) says that equal-rank pairing maximizes \(E(XY)\), whereas reverse-rank pairing minimizes it. By (1), equal-rank pairing therefore minimizes the quadratic cost and reverse-rank pairing maximizes it. This proves the two formulas in \(\mathrm{def:twoarm\text{-}sorting}\).

For general fixed \(K\), label every atom of every observed empirical margin, even when two labels carry the same numerical residual. A coupling of the labeled empirical measures assigns a mass \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\) to each tuple
\((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\). Its \(a\)-th marginal is \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\) if and only if
\[
\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}
\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}
\tag{2}
\]
for every \(a\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\). Thus the feasible arrays in \(\mathrm{def:fixed\text{-}k\text{-}lp}\) are exactly all couplings of the empirical margins, and the displayed LP objective is exactly
\[
\int\left(\sum_{a=1}^Kc_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the product coupling, and it is a compact polytope because (2), nonnegativity, and total mass one define a closed bounded subset of a finite-dimensional space. The linear objective consequently attains its minimum and maximum, which are respectively \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\) by \(\mathrm{def:transport\text{-}values}\). The cited finite multi-marginal Kantorovich duality result \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}mot\text{-}kantorovich\text{-}duality}\) equates the minimum with its finite dual. Applying the same result to the negative cost and multiplying both primal and dual values by \(-1\) proves the corresponding equality for the maximum. Hence both programs give exact convexified empirical endpoints.

It remains to prove the replication assertion, which is specific to this proposition. The constraints in (2) have rational coefficients and rational right-hand sides. A linear functional on a nonempty polytope has an optimal face containing an extreme point; every extreme point of this rational polytope is rational because its coordinates solve a full-rank subsystem of the active rational equalities. Thus a rational optimal plan exists. More generally, let \(\pi\) be any rational optimal plan. Put \(N=\sum_am_{nba}=n_{nb}\), and choose an integer \(L\) divisible by \(N\), by every \(m_{nba}\), and by every denominator occurring among the finitely many values \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\). Create
\[
L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}
\]
replicated units of joint type \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\). These multiplicities are nonnegative integers and sum to \(L\). By (2), the arm-\(a\) label \(i_a\) occurs exactly
\[
\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}}L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}
=\frac{L}{m_{nba}}
\tag{3}
\]
times. Therefore, within arm \(a\), every label is replicated by the integer factor \(L/m_{nba}\), and the empirical joint law on the replicated common unit labels is exactly \(\pi\). Set the replicated complete-randomization quota to \(m_{nba}'=(L/N)m_{nba}\); these are positive integers, preserve the original arm fractions, and sum to \(L\). Assigning to each replicated unit the corresponding centered armwise residual values, and choosing fixed potential outcomes and nodewise predictable fitted values whose difference equals those residuals, realizes the plan at that single history node. Repeating the construction at integer multiples of \(L\) gives nodewise completion attainability along growing replicated block sizes. The construction neither retains the original unreplicated block size nor enforces compatibility with any other history node, exactly as the proposition states.

As the smallest arithmetic stress test, take both centered lists to be \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\). For the unnormalized contrast \((1,-1)\), equal-rank pairing makes the squared contrast identically zero, while reverse-rank pairing makes it identically four. Hence the two costs are \(0\) and \(4\), and for a block of size four the associated envelope width is
\[
\frac{4w_{nb}^2}{4-1}>0.
\]
For the normalized contrast \((1,-1)/\sqrt2\), both costs and this width are divided by two. This verifies both the endpoint ordering and nontrivial width.

semantic_closure.name: \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\)
semantic_closure.construction: \[\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\left\{\Xi_n=\left((Y_{nbi}(a))_{b,i,a},(m_{nba}^{h})_{b,h,a},(g_{nbi}^{h}(a))_{b,h,i,a}\right):\begin{array}{l}(Y_{nbi}(a))_{b,i,a}\text{ is fixed before randomization};\\ (m_{nba}^{h})_{a\in\mathcal A}\text{ and }(g_{nbi}^{h}(a))_{i,a}\text{ are the evaluations of the same prespecified predictable allocation and fitting rules at every }h;\\ \text{for every }b\le B_n\text{ and }h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\ R_{nbi}^{h}(a)=Y_{nbi}(a)-g_{nbi}^{h}(a)\text{ has centered margins }\mu_{nba}^{h};\\ \gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\delta_{(R_{nbi}^{h}(1)-\bar R_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,R_{nbi}^{h}(K)-\bar R_{nbK}^{h})}\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\end{array}\right\}.\] Thus one member fixes common unit labels and all potential outcomes before assignment and induces the counts, fitted values, residual margins, feasible couplings, and transport endpoints at every node, including nodes off the realized path.

semantic_closure.name: \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n),\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n),U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)\)
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), let \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\) be its nodewise conditional-variance contribution. With the predictable block weight already included in \(U_{nb}^{h}\) and \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\), define the normalized root-to-leaf compatibility gap
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}\ \sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}\frac1{s_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\left\{U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}-Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}\right\}.
\]
Define the single-node multi-index integrality diagnostic
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\sup_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}\left[\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma-J_{nb}^{h,-}\right].
\]
For a fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\), define the reduced nodewise contribution \(U_{nb}^{h,\rho}=(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h}\) and the corresponding root-to-leaf endpoint
\[
U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi),\rho}.
\]
The two gaps and \(U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)\) are retained only for the unresolved global history-tree compatibility problem; the fixed-fraction necessity result for uniform inference is certified separately by an explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass.

semantic_closure.name: Residual history-tree integer-flow handle
semantic_closure.construction: The fixed-fraction necessity direction for uniform inference is settled by the explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass in \(\text{thm:fixed-fraction-upper-endpoint-necessity}\). The remaining handle concerns only global adaptive-history compatibility: represent one ex ante sequence \((\Xi_n)_{n\ge1}\), with \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) and its entire induced triangular experiment-analysis array in \(\mathfrak D\), as a history-tree integer multi-index flow with common unit labels. Enforce prefix consistency by backward induction and compare its root-to-leaf objective with \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\). Use rational replication at an isolated node to measure \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), then characterize the additional loss caused by sharing one fixed potential-outcome array and one predictable fitting rule across incompatible branches while preserving membership in \(\mathfrak D\).

carrier.proof_tex:
We construct the subclass explicitly. Fix \(K\ge2\), a zero-sum contrast satisfying \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\), and set
\[
q_n=2n,\qquad B_n=n^3,
\qquad n_{nb}=Kq_n,qquad m_{nba}=q_n,qquad w_{nb}=B_n^{-1}
\tag{1}
\]
for every \(b\le B_n\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\). In each block label exactly \(Kq_n/2\) units by \(x_i=-1\) and the remaining \(Kq_n/2\) units by \(x_i=1\), and define
\[
Y_{nbi}(a)=x_i\quad\text{for every }a,
\qquad g_{nbi}(a)=0.
\tag{2}
\]
The parity in (2) is valid because \(q_n=2n\). Use the nonadaptive complete-block design that is uniform over assignments with the quotas in (1). This gives fixed potential outcomes, consistency, predictable counts, complete-block randomization, and predictable zero adjustments. The arm fraction is \(1/K\), so overlap holds, for example, with the common constant \(\varepsilon_0=1/(2K)\). The residuals equal \(x_i\) and obey \(|R_{nbi}(a)|=1\), so the residual-moment condition holds with any fixed \(\delta_0>0\) and \(C_R=1\). The count lower bound is exactly \(q_n\to\infty\).

Every arm has the same centered residual marginal
\[
\mu_{nba}=\tfrac12\delta_{-1}+\tfrac12\delta_1,
\qquad S_{nba}^2=\frac{Kq_n}{Kq_n-1}=:S_n^2.
\tag{3}
\]
Coupling all arm coordinates identically, \(x_1=\cdots=x_K\), is feasible and has quadratic contrast cost
\[
\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2=x_1^2\left(\sum_ac_a\right)^2=0.
\]
The cost is nonnegative, hence \(J_{nb}^{-}=0\). The common unit labels in (2) induce exactly this zero-cost coupling, so the conditional-variance identity in \(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}predictable\text{-}ot\text{-}envelope}\) gives, block by block,
\[
E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\frac1{B_n^2}\sum_a\frac{c_a^2S_n^2}{q_n}
=\frac{S_n^2}{B_n^2q_n}=U_{nb}.
\tag{4}
\]
Therefore
\[
V_n=U_n=\frac{S_n^2}{B_nq_n}
\quad\text{deterministically}.
\tag{5}
\]
In particular, the predictable quadratic variation stabilizes exactly at its expectation. Moreover,
\[
s_n^2=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\frac{B_n^{-2}}{Kq_n}
=\frac1{B_nKq_n},
\qquad
\frac{V_n}{s_n^2}=KS_n^2\ge K,
\tag{6}
\]
so predictable-QV growth holds with, for example, \(v_0=1\). If \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\), then
\[
\max_{b\le B_n}\frac{t_{nb}}{s_n^2}=\frac1{B_n}=n^{-3}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{7}
\]
which verifies block leverage with \(\ell_n=B_n^{-1}\). Thus the construction is a nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass of one common-parameter admissible class.

We verify the martingale central limit theorem rather than assume it. Since every armwise sample mean lies in \([-1,1]\), contrast normalization and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
|D_{nb}|\le B_n^{-1}\sum_a|c_a|le\frac{\sqrt K}{B_n}.
\tag{8}
\]
With \(\sigma_n^2=E(V_n)=V_n\), equations (1), (3), and (5) imply
\[
\max_b\frac{|D_{nb}|}{\sigma_n}
\le\sqrt{\frac{Kq_n}{B_nS_n^2}}
\le\sqrt{\frac{Kq_n}{B_n}}
=\frac{\sqrt{2K}}{n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{9}
\]
Hence, for every \(\epsilon>0\), the conditional Lindeberg sum in \(\mathrm{lem:martingale\text{-}clt\text{-}predictable\text{-}variation}\) is identically zero for all sufficiently large \(n\); (5) supplies its predictable-variation condition. Since \(\tau_n=0\) by \(\sum_ac_a=0\), that lemma and the AIPW decomposition yield
\[
T_n:=\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\tag{10}
\]

The already proved history-uniform plug-in theorem applies to this admissible subclass. Because \(V_n=U_n\ge Ks_n^2\), it gives
\[
\frac{|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{V_n}
\le\frac1K\frac{|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus \(\widehat U_n/V_n\to1\) in probability. Combining (10)--(11), the random-threshold form of Slutsky's argument and continuity of the standard normal law give, for every fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr\!\left\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|
\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n}\right\}
&=\Pr\!\left\{|T_n|
\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n/V_n}\right\}\\
&\longrightarrow
2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\rho}\right)-1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Because \(z_{1-\alpha/2}>0\), \(0<\sqrt{1-\rho}<1\), and \(\Phi\) is strictly increasing, the limit in (12) is strictly smaller than
\(2\Phi(z_{1-\alpha/2})-1=1-\alpha\).

For the required smallest exact check, take \(K=2\), \(q_n=2\), one block, \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), and the common list \((-1,-1,1,1)\). Among the \(\binom42=6\) assignments of arm one, the value of \(D_{n1}\) is \(-\sqrt2\) once, \(0\) four times, and \(\sqrt2\) once. Its exact variance is therefore \(2/3\), while (3)--(4) give \(S_n^2/q_n=(4/3)/2=2/3\) and \(J_{n1}^{-}=0\). Thus the asserted equality \(V_n=U_n\) survives exhaustive enumeration of the smallest nontrivial block.

Finally, if a broader design family contains this subclass, its rowwise worst-case coverage is an infimum over a set containing the constructed row and is therefore no larger than the probability in (12). Taking the limsup proves the advertised upper bound. The construction is nonadaptive and globally fixed, so this certificate uses no simultaneous selection of optimizers across distinct adaptive history nodes.

target_declaration.statement:
There exists a nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass of an admissible common-parameter class \(\mathfrak D\) with \(B_n\to\infty\), \(q_n\to\infty\), equal block weights \(w_{nb}=B_n^{-1}\), block sizes \(n_{nb}=Kq_n\), equal quotas \(m_{nba}=q_n\), zero adjustments \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), and identical bounded potential-outcome lists across arms, such that \(J_{nb}^{-}=0\) in every block and \(V_n=U_n\) deterministically. This subclass satisfies the full overlap, residual-moment, count-growth, block-leverage, predictable-QV growth, predictable-QV stabilization, endpoint-consistency, and martingale-CLT conditions. Consequently, for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n}\right\}
 \longrightarrow
 2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\rho}\right)-1
 <1-\alpha.
\]
Therefore, for any broader design family containing this subclass, the limsup of its worst-case coverage after replacing \(\widehat U_n\) by \((1-\rho)\widehat U_n\) is at most the displayed strict sub-nominal limit. This is a fixed-quota subclass converse for uniform inference, not a claim that independently selected nodewise transport optimizers are jointly realizable by one completion over an adaptive history tree.
target_declaration.justification: An explicit admissible fixed-quota sequence makes the transport upper endpoint equal the true predictable quadratic variation and supplies a matching fixed-fraction undercoverage certificate.
target_declaration.gap: Nodewise completion attainability is not needed for this inference converse; the remaining unsolved issue is simultaneous compatibility across an adaptive history tree.
target_declaration.consumer: The result certifies that a batched quota-controlled trial cannot uniformly shorten the transport-based standard error by any fixed fraction, even on the simplest nonadaptive subfamily.

semantic_closure.statement: For every array in \(\mathfrak D\), \((M_{nj},\mathcal F_{n,j})_{j\le B_n}\) is a martingale and \[E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac1{n_{nb}-1}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\right\},\] where \(\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\in\Gamma_{nb}\) is the joint centered residual coupling in block \(b\). At every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}\), the conditional variance range over \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\) has endpoints obtained from \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\) and \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\), and both endpoints are attained within that node's convexified coupling set. Evaluating these nodewise endpoints along the realized pre-block histories yields the predictable pathwise containment \(V_n\in[L_n,U_n]\). For any fixed root-to-leaf path, independent selection of feasible couplings at its visited nodes attains both summed endpoints in the rectangular relaxation \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\). Thus the interval is exact only nodewise and path by path inside that rectangular convexified relaxation. This theorem does not assert that one globally consistent fixed-potential-outcome adaptive-history completion realizes independently selected optimizers across different nodes. When \(B_n=1\) and \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), direct substitution gives the static quadratic MOT variance formula of Gao, Ge, and Qian. When \(B_n\ge2\) and counts respond to earlier outcomes, \([L_n,U_n]\) is a sum of pre-block-measurable random endpoints rather than one static MOT functional, and the claim does not condition on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Put \(r=4+\delta_0\), and fix an arbitrary pre-block history \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\). Membership in the common-parameter class specified by \(\text{def:admissible-arrays}\), together with \(\text{ass:predictable-adjustment}\), makes the potential outcomes, count vector, fitting values, and residual lists in block \(b\) fixed at this conditioning event. For one arm \(a\), abbreviate
\[
X_i=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba},\qquad N=n_{nb},\qquad m=m_{nba}.
\]
Jensen's inequality and \(\text{ass:residual-moments}\) give
\[
\frac1N\sum_i|X_i|^r
\le 2^{r-1}\left\{\frac1N\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^r+|\bar R_{nba}|^r\right\}
\le 2^r C_R.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\text{ass:consistency-no-interference}\), the residual observed on a label assigned to arm \(a\) is \(R_{nbi}(a)\). By \(\text{ass:complete-block-randomization}\), the arm-\(a\) labels form a simple random sample without replacement of size \(m\) from the \(N\) labels.

Define the population-centered sample and population measures
\[
\nu=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}\delta_{X_i},
\qquad
\mu=\frac1N\sum_i\delta_{X_i}=\mu_{nba}.
\]
For \(T>0\), clip both measures to \([-T,T]\), partition that interval into \(H\) cells of length at most \(2T/H\), and project each cell to one representative. If \(P_h\) and \(\widehat P_h\) are the population and sample masses of cell \(h\), the first- and second-order inclusion probabilities under simple random sampling give
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat P_h\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\frac{N-m}{m(N-1)}P_h(1-P_h)\le\frac1{4m}.
\]
Therefore, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
E\left(\sum_{h=1}^H|\widehat P_h-P_h|\middle|\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)
\le\frac{H}{2\sqrt m}.
\tag{2}
\]
Match projected mass inside each cell and move unmatched clipped mass across a distance at most \(2T\). The within-cell squared cost is at most \(4T^2/H^2\), while the unmatched squared cost is at most a universal constant times \(T^2\sum_h|\widehat P_h-P_h|\). Moreover, (1) and
\(X_i^2\mathbf 1\{|X_i|>T\}\le |X_i|^rT^{-(r-2)}\) bound the population clipping cost by \(2^rC_RT^{-(r-2)}\); its conditional sample expectation is the same by the first-order inclusion probability. Applying the triangle inequality for \(W_2\), and absorbing the numerical factors into \(C=C(r,C_R)\), yields
\[
E\{W_2^2(\nu,\mu)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C\left(\frac{T^2}{H^2}+\frac{T^2H}{\sqrt m}+T^{-(r-2)}\right).
\tag{3}
\]
Choose \(H=\lceil m^{1/6}\rceil\) and \(T=m^{1/(3r)}\). Each term on the right of (3) is at most a constant times \(m^{-\beta}\), where
\[
\beta=\frac{r-2}{3r}.
\tag{4}
\]

The observable measure \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\) is the translate of \(\nu\) by minus the sample mean \(\bar X_S=m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i\). Since \(N^{-1}\sum_iX_i=0\), the exact simple-random-sampling covariance identity gives
\[
E(\bar X_S^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2\le\frac{C}{m},
\tag{5}
\]
where the last inequality follows from (1). Translation by a scalar admits a coupling of squared cost equal to the squared scalar. The triangle inequality for \(W_2\), (3)--(5), and \(0<\beta<1\) imply
\[
E\{W_2^2(\widehat\mu_{nba},\mu_{nba})\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C m_{nba}^{-\beta}.
\tag{6}
\]

For the diagonal variance term, write
\[
\overline{X^2}_S=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i^2,
\qquad
\overline{X^2}=\frac1N\sum_iX_i^2.
\]
The same sampling covariance identity, now applied to the finite list \((X_i^2)_i\), and (1) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E\{|\overline{X^2}_S-\overline{X^2}|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
&\le\left\{\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)
\frac1{N-1}\sum_i(X_i^2-\overline{X^2})^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
&\le C m^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
For \(m,N\ge2\),
\[
\widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac{m}{m-1}(\overline{X^2}_S-\bar X_S^2),
\qquad
S_{nba}^2=\frac{N}{N-1}\overline{X^2}.
\]
Equations (5)--(7), \(|m/(m-1)-1|\le2/m\), \(|N/(N-1)-1|\le2/N\), and the second-moment consequence of (1) therefore show
\[
E\{|\widehat S_{nba}^2-S_{nba}^2|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C m_{nba}^{-1/2}.
\tag{8}
\]

It remains to control the multi-marginal values. For every arm, choose an optimal quadratic coupling between \(\mu_{nba}\) and \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\). These couplings exist because both measures have finite support. Starting from any \(\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}\), disintegrate the pairwise couplings and draw the empirical coordinates conditionally on their corresponding population coordinates. If \(X\) has law \(\gamma\) and \(Y\) is the resulting vector, then \(Y\) has the empirical armwise marginals and
\(E(X_a-Y_a)^2=W_2^2(\mu_{nba},\widehat\mu_{nba})\). By \(\text{ass:contrast-normalization}\) and Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
\begin{aligned}
|E(c^\top X)^2-E(c^\top Y)^2|
&\le\{E(c^\top(X-Y))^2\}^{1/2}
\{E(c^\top(X+Y))^2\}^{1/2}\\
&\le\left\{\sum_aW_2^2(\mu_{nba},\widehat\mu_{nba})\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{2\sum_a(EX_a^2+EY_a^2)\right\}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Apply (9) first to an optimizer for the population coupling polytope and then, with the roles reversed, to an optimizer for the empirical polytope. This bounds both differences of infima and both differences of suprema. Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz, (1), (6), and the corresponding expected second-moment bound for the empirical margins give, for either sign,
\[
E\{|\widehat J_{nb}^{\pm}-J_{nb}^{\pm}|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C\left(\min_a m_{nba}\right)^{-\beta/2}.
\tag{10}
\]
No uniqueness of an optimizer is required.

Let \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\), so \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\). By \(\text{ass:overlap}\), \(m_{nba}^{-1}\le(\varepsilon_0n_{nb})^{-1}\), and \((n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\le2n_{nb}^{-1}\) when \(n_{nb}\ge2\). Combining (8), (10), \(\text{def:qv-envelope}\), and \(\text{def:plugin-envelope}\), then summing the absolute block errors and applying the tower property under the original sequential assignment law, gives whenever every arm count is at least two,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
E_{\mathbb D}\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}
&\le\frac{C}{s_n^2}\sum_bt_{nb}
\left(q_n^{-1/2}+q_n^{-\beta/2}\right)\\
&\le Cq_n^{-\kappa},
\qquad
\kappa=\frac\beta2=\frac{2+\delta_0}{6(4+\delta_0)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
The conditional constants are uniform over every possible pre-block history because all primitive envelopes are common over \(\mathfrak D\). Thus (11) uses neither a union bound over histories nor a union bound over blocks; the tower property integrates each realized pre-block history rather than conditioning on the terminal path.

If some arm count is below two, \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) implies \(q_n<2\). The truncated loss is at most one, while \(1\le2^\kappa q_n^{-\kappa}\). Enlarging the constant by \(2^\kappa\) therefore covers every \(n\), including the total-convention cases. Hence
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}\left[1\wedge
\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\right]
\le C_{\mathrm{ep}}q_n^{-\kappa}=C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n,
\tag{12}
\]
where \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}\) depends only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\).

For every nonnegative \(X\) and every \(\eta>0\),
\(\mathbf1\{X>\eta\}\le(1\wedge X)/(1\wedge\eta)\). Applying this inequality to the normalized summed endpoint error in (12) gives the asserted probability bound. The Hausdorff distance between two real intervals is
\(\max\{|\widehat L_n-L_n|,|\widehat U_n-U_n|\}\), which is no larger than their summed endpoint error, proving its stated bound with the same constant. Finally, \(q_n\to\infty\) and \(\kappa>0\) imply \(r_n\to0\). Every expectation and probability above is taken under the original sequential randomization law, with conditioning only on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), never on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \((D_{nb})_{b\le B_n}\) be a triangular array of square-integrable martingale differences with respect to the pre-increment histories \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), let \(V_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\), and put \(\sigma_n^2=E(V_n)>0\).  If \(V_n/\sigma_n^2\to1\) in probability and, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\frac1{\sigma_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E\left[D_{nb}^2\mathbf 1\{|D_{nb}|>\epsilon\sigma_n\}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right]\to0
\quad\text{in probability},
\]
then \(\sigma_n^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}D_{nb}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\).

source.locator: Supplementary Material, Lemma S4, which reviews Brown (1971), Theorem 2; see also Hall and Heyde (2014), Corollary 3.1
source.verbatim_statement: Let {xi_Tt in R, F_Tt: 1 <= t <= T, T >= 1} be an array of square-integrable martingale difference sequences. Let Vcheck_T = sum_t E(xi_Tt^2 | F_T,t-1), where F_T0 is empty; V_T = E(Vcheck_T). As T tends to infinity, if (i) Vcheck_T/V_T = 1 + o_P(1); (ii) V_T^{-1} sum_t E{xi_Tt^2 1(|xi_Tt| >= epsilon V_T^{-1/2})} = o_P(1) for all epsilon > 0, then V_T^{-1/2} sum_t xi_Tt converges in distribution to N(0,1).

semantic_closure.name: \(\mathfrak E_M(K,\varepsilon_0,M,(q_n))\)
semantic_closure.construction:
For the endpoint-only rate statement, let \(\mathfrak E_M(K,\varepsilon_0,M,(q_n))\) be the class of the same triangular experiment-analysis arrays for which \(K\) is fixed, \(q_n\to\infty\), the common bound
\[
\sup_{n\ge1}\max_{b\le B_n}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}
\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\max_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|\le M
\]
holds, and the member properties \(\text{ass:fixed-potential-outcomes}\), \(\text{ass:consistency-no-interference}\), \(\text{ass:predictable-counts}\), \(\text{ass:complete-block-randomization}\), \(\text{ass:predictable-adjustment}\), \(\text{ass:overlap}\), \(\text{ass:contrast-zero-sum}\), \(\text{ass:contrast-normalization}\), and \(\text{ass:growing-arm-counts}\) hold with the displayed common parameters. No residual-moment, block-leverage, or predictable-quadratic-variation condition is included in \(\mathfrak E_M\). By construction, \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak E_M\).

semantic_closure.name: \(\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a),\widehat S_{nba}^2,\widehat\mu_{nba}\)
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\) of observed size \(|\mathcal O_{nba}|=m_{nba}\), define
\[
\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\},\qquad \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},
\]
\[
\widehat\mu_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)},\qquad \widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac1{m_{nba}-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2.
\]
Set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) and \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=0\), and set \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=1\). These total conventions are inactive for the endpoint theorem for all sufficiently large \(n\), because \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) and \(q_n\to\infty\).

semantic_closure.statement: For sequences of ex ante margin systems \(\boldsymbol\mu_n\) with \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\ne\varnothing\), characterize necessary and sufficient conditions for \[\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}\sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}\frac1{s_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\{U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}-Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}\}\longrightarrow0.\] The characterization must separate the single-node multi-index obstruction measured by \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) from the additional cross-history obstruction created by common unit labels, fixed potential outcomes, and one predictable fitting rule across incompatible branches. For the inference consequence, restrict attention to a single sequence \((\Xi_n)_{n\ge1}\), fixed ex ante, such that \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) for every \(n\) and the sequential experiment-analysis array induced by the entire sequence belongs to \(\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))\). Thus the same sequence inherits fixed potential outcomes, consistency, predictable fixed counts followed by complete-block randomization, predictable adjustment, common overlap, normalized zero-sum contrast, deterministic arm-count growth, leverage control, residual moments, observable plug-in endpoint consistency, predictable-QV nondegeneracy, and the uniform martingale central limit theorem. Determine whether, under the zero-gap conditions, for every fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\) there is such an admissible sequence satisfying \[\sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}\frac1{s_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\{U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}-Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}\}\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)+o(1)\] for which the oracle path reduction \(U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}\), estimated along the endogenous path by \((1-\rho)\widehat U_n\), satisfies \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{\Xi_n}\left\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n}\right\}<1-\alpha.\] Neither the completion sequence nor its nodewise couplings may be selected using \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\).
semantic_closure.justification: The normalized minimax gap makes the compatibility problem testable, keeps nodewise integrality distinct from cross-history consistency, and admits an inferential consequence only through completion sequences in the full common-parameter class.
semantic_closure.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance proves static completion sharpness, and GaoGeQian2025MOT permits fractional multi-marginal plans; neither characterizes when one fixed finite-population completion implements a rectangular family of optimizers consistently across an adaptive history tree.
semantic_closure.consumer: A zero-gap characterization with an admissible-class attainment theorem would certify when no fixed-fraction shortening of the residual-marginal Wald interval remains uniformly valid in predictably batched adaptive trials.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every fixed \(M>0\), there is a constant \(C_M<\infty\), depending only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,M\), such that for every \(n\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak E_M}E_{\mathbb D}\left[1\wedge
\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\right]
\le C_Mq_n^{-1/2}.
\]
Consequently the same bound holds with \(\mathfrak E_M\) replaced by the bounded-residual subclass \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak D\), and the normalized endpoint error converges to zero uniformly on either class. The bound has no dependence on \(B_n\), contains no logarithmic history factor, and requires no block-leverage condition. It is unconditional under the original sequential randomization and never freezes the terminal adaptive path.
semantic_closure.justification: The bounded-support subclass exposes a genuine parametric endpoint-rate elbow while preserving the general moment-only theorem unchanged.
semantic_closure.gap: The static bounded-iid transport benchmark does not prove a history-uniform finite-population result under predictable quotas and sampling without replacement.
semantic_closure.consumer: A predictably batched trial with a common history-uniform residual bound obtains endpoint error of order \(q_n^{-1/2}\) without any dependence on the number of blocks, any logarithmic history factor, or a block-leverage requirement for endpoint estimation.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbb D\in\mathfrak E_M\), a block \(b\), and a pre-block history \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\). The class definition makes the count vector, fitting values, potential outcomes, and residual lists fixed at this node. For an arm \(a\), write
\[
X_i=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba},\qquad N=n_{nb},\qquad m=m_{nba},
\]
and let \(\mu=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{X_i}=\mu_{nba}\) and
\(\nu=m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}\delta_{X_i}\). The bounded-residual condition gives
\[
|X_i|\le |R_{nbi}(a)|+|\bar R_{nba}|\le2M.
\tag{1}
\]
Consistency identifies the sampled residuals, and conditional complete randomization makes the arm-\(a\) labels a simple random sample without replacement of size \(m\).

We first prove the required one-dimensional finite-population empirical-measure bound. Let \(F\) and \(\widehat F\) be the distribution functions of \(\mu\) and \(\nu\). For each \(t\in\mathbb R\), the exact inclusion-probability calculation for the finite list \((\mathbf1\{X_i\le t\})_{i=1}^N\) gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}\{\widehat F(t)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
=\frac{N-m}{m(N-1)}F(t)\{1-F(t)\}\le\frac1{4m}.
\tag{2}
\]
For completeness, for finitely supported probability measures on the line, order all atoms jointly. Across the interval between two consecutive atom locations, every transport plan must move at least the absolute cumulative mass imbalance across that cut. The greedy increasing matching moves exactly that imbalance and no more. Summing interval length times cumulative imbalance proves directly that
\[
W_1(\nu,\mu)=\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat F(t)-F(t)|\,dt.
\tag{3}
\]
This is a finite matching identity, not an imported empirical-process theorem. By (1), the integrand in (3) vanishes outside \([-2M,2M]\). Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and (2) therefore give
\[
E\{W_1(\nu,\mu)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le\int_{-2M}^{2M}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\widehat F(t)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})}\,dt
\le\frac{2M}{\sqrt m}.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(\bar X_S=m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i\). Since the population mean of the \(X_i\)'s is zero, the simple-random-sampling covariance identity and (1) imply
\[
E(\bar X_S^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2
\le\frac{8M^2}{m}.
\tag{5}
\]
The observable margin is exactly
\(\widehat\mu_{nba}=T_{-\bar X_S\,\#}\nu\), because subtracting the observed residual mean sends \(X_i\) to \(X_i-\bar X_S\). Coupling every atom with its translate, then using (4), (5), and the triangle inequality, yields the observable-centering bound
\[
E\{W_1(\widehat\mu_{nba},\mu_{nba})\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le (2+2\sqrt2)M m_{nba}^{-1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]

The sample-variance term has the same parametric order. Put
\[
A_S=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i^2,
\qquad A=\frac1N\sum_iX_i^2.
\]
Since \(0\le X_i^2\le4M^2\), the sampling covariance identity gives
\[
E(|A_S-A|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
\le\left\{\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)
\frac1{N-1}\sum_i(X_i^2-A)^2\right\}^{1/2}
\le4\sqrt2 M^2m^{-1/2}.
\tag{7}
\]
For \(m,N\ge2\),
\[
\widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac{m}{m-1}(A_S-\bar X_S^2),
\qquad S_{nba}^2=\frac{N}{N-1}A.
\]
Using (5), (7), \(m/(m-1)\le2\), \(A\le4M^2\), and
\(|m/(m-1)-N/(N-1)|\le2/m\), we obtain a numerical constant \(C_0\) such that
\[
E\{|\widehat S_{nba}^2-S_{nba}^2|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C_0M^2m_{nba}^{-1/2}.
\tag{8}
\]

We next prove bounded-support Lipschitz sensitivity of the fixed-\(K\) multi-marginal objective. Let \(\phi(x)=(c^\top x)^2\). If \(x,y\in[-2M,2M]^K\), contrast normalization implies \(\|c\|_1\le\sqrt K\) and \(|c_a|\le1\), so
\[
|\phi(x)-\phi(y)|
=|c^\top(x-y)|\,|c^\top(x+y)|
\le4M\sqrt K\sum_{a=1}^K|x_a-y_a|.
\tag{9}
\]
For each arm, take an optimal \(W_1\) coupling between \(\mu_{nba}\) and \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\). Glue its conditional kernel to any coupling of the population margins. The resulting vector has the empirical margins, and (9) bounds the change in expected cost by
\[
4M\sqrt K\sum_{a=1}^K W_1(\mu_{nba},\widehat\mu_{nba}).
\]
Apply this construction to a population minimizer and maximizer and then reverse the roles of the population and empirical margins. The finite coupling polytopes are compact, so all four optimizers exist. Equation (6) thus gives, for either sign, a constant \(C_1=C_1(K,M)\) such that
\[
E\{|\widehat J_{nb}^{\pm}-J_{nb}^{\pm}|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C_1\left(\min_a m_{nba}\right)^{-1/2}.
\tag{10}
\]

Let \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\). When every arm count is at least two, overlap, count growth, and \((n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\le2n_{nb}^{-1}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
&E\bigl[|\widehat L_{nb}-L_{nb}|+|\widehat U_{nb}-U_{nb}|
\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\bigr]\\
&\qquad\le
C_2w_{nb}^2\left\{
\sum_a\frac{c_a^2M^2m_{nba}^{-1/2}}{m_{nba}}
+\frac{M^2(\min_am_{nba})^{-1/2}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\}\\
&\qquad\le C_3t_{nb}q_n^{-1/2},
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
where \(L_{nb},U_{nb},\widehat L_{nb},\widehat U_{nb}\) denote the corresponding block summands in the two envelope definitions. In the last line we used \(m_{nba}^{-1}\le(\varepsilon_0n_{nb})^{-1}\), \(m_{nba}^{-1/2}\le q_n^{-1/2}\), \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\), and absorbed the fixed \(K\) into \(C_3=C_3(K,\varepsilon_0,M)\).

The bound (11) is valid at every pre-block history with the same constant. Summing it, applying the tower property along the original adaptive filtration, and using \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\) gives
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak E_M}
E_{\mathbb D}\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}
\le C_Mq_n^{-1/2}.
\tag{12}
\]
No maximum over history nodes, union bound, or conditioning on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\) occurs. Consequently neither \(B_n\) nor a logarithmic history factor appears, and no block-leverage condition has been used. If an arm count is below two, then \(q_n<2\); since the theorem truncates the normalized loss at one, increasing \(C_M\) by a universal factor covers these finitely indexed convention cases. This proves the displayed theorem for every \(n\). Finally, \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak E_M\) by the two class definitions, so the same bound holds over \(\mathfrak D_M\), and \(q_n\to\infty\) proves uniform convergence on both classes.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), restrict attention to arrays in the displayed common-parameter class \(\mathfrak D\) for which \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}stabilization}\) additionally holds uniformly. This is an explicit load-bearing high-level regularity condition and is not derived from predictable quotas, complete-block randomization, overlap, growing arm counts, leverage, residual moments, or QV growth. On that restricted class, \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.\] More precisely, the common leverage envelope \(\ell_n\to0\), the common residual-moment envelope \((\delta_0,C_R)\), the finite-population nondegeneracy condition \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\), together with this additional uniform predictable-QV stabilization, imply \((\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)/\sqrt{V_n}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\) uniformly. The nodewise rectangular envelope gives \(V_n\le U_n\) pathwise, and the explicit bound \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n=o(1)\) permits \(U_n\) to be replaced by \(\widehat U_n\). No conditioning on the terminal adaptive path is required.
semantic_closure.justification: The theorem converts the nodewise rectangular upper variance endpoint into unconditional conservative design-based coverage under a separately imposed uniform predictable-QV stabilization condition.

LiZhao2026AdaptiveDesignBased, CookMishlerRamdas2024AdaptiveInference, and HadadEtAl2021AdaptiveExperiments establish adaptive inference under their own designs and normalizations, but none supplies this finite-population complete-block residual-coupling endpoint or its history-uniform plug-in bound.

semantic_closure.name: Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}

semantic_closure.condition: Conditional on baseline information, the array \(\{Y_{nbi}(a):b\le B_n,\ i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\ a\in\mathcal A\}\) is nonrandom under the assignment law.

novel.justification: This is an explicit fixed-count complete-block design restriction of the paper. It is implementable in predictably batched platform experiments that update integer arm quotas after each completed batch and then use uniform complete randomization within the next batch; minimum cell sizes and capacity caps can be enforced directly by the quota rule. Li and Zhao's broader block-adaptive framework is not cited as supplying this restriction.

semantic_closure.condition: The array \((g_{nbi}(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
The predictable arm fractions satisfy \(\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0\) almost surely for every \(n\), \(b\), and \(a\).
The predictable counts satisfy \(\min_{b\le B_n,\,a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) almost surely for every \(n\), where the deterministic lower-count envelope obeys \(q_n\to\infty\).
The design leverage satisfies \(\max_{b\le B_n}\{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\}/s_n^2\le\ell_n\) for every \(n\).
The nuisance-adjusted residual arrays satisfy \(\sup_{n,b,a}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\le C_R\).
The predictable quadratic variation satisfies \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\) almost surely for every \(n\).

novel.justification: This common finite-population condition excludes asymptotically deterministic contrasts while allowing heterogeneous residual couplings; it holds, for example, when each root-to-leaf path contains a fixed share of blocks with residual contrast variance bounded below relative to \(s_n^2\).

semantic_closure.statement: The constructions in \(\text{def:twoarm-sorting}\) equal \(J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(J_{nb}^{+}\) for \(K=2\). For each fixed \(K\), feeding the observable assigned-arm measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)}\) into the finite primal programs in \(\text{def:fixed-k-lp}\) attains \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\), and their Kantorovich duals have the same values. These are exact convexified empirical endpoints. At any single history node, every rational optimal plan is realized by a deterministic fixed-potential-outcome block completion after finite replication of that node's armwise lists, so its LP endpoints are asymptotically nodewise completion-attainable as block sizes grow. No same-size integrality assertion for \(K>2\), and no cross-history assertion that one \(\Xi_n\) realizes independently chosen nodewise plans, is made.
semantic_closure.justification: The result turns the abstract envelope into sorting for two arms and a finite auditable computation for multiple arms.
semantic_closure.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance gives two-arm rearrangement, while GaoGeQian2025MOT gives static MOT computation; neither states the finite-population replication boundary needed for adaptive design-based sharpness.
semantic_closure.consumer: A four-arm complete-block redesign of the NewbyEtAl2025MentalHealth minitrials can compute each endpoint using a fixed-\(K\) transportation program.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For \(K=2\) and \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), the identity
\[
\frac12(x-y)^2=\frac12x^2+\frac12y^2-xy
\tag{1}
\]
shows that the two marginal square terms do not depend on the coupling. The cited rearrangement result \(\mathrm{lem:twoarm\text{-}rearrangement\text{-}extrema}\) says that equal-rank pairing maximizes \(E(XY)\), whereas reverse-rank pairing minimizes it. By (1), equal-rank pairing therefore minimizes the quadratic cost and reverse-rank pairing maximizes it. This proves the two formulas in \(\mathrm{def:twoarm\text{-}sorting}\).

For general fixed \(K\), label every atom of every observed empirical margin, even when two labels carry the same numerical residual. A coupling of the labeled empirical measures assigns a mass \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\) to each tuple
\((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\). Its \(a\)-th marginal is \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\) if and only if
\[
\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}
\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}
\tag{2}
\]
for every \(a\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\). Thus the feasible arrays in \(\mathrm{def:fixed\text{-}k\text{-}lp}\) are exactly all couplings of the empirical margins, and the displayed LP objective is exactly
\[
\int\left(\sum_{a=1}^Kc_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the product coupling, and it is a compact polytope because (2), nonnegativity, and total mass one define a closed bounded subset of a finite-dimensional space. The linear objective consequently attains its minimum and maximum, which are respectively \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\) by \(\mathrm{def:transport\text{-}values}\). The cited finite multi-marginal Kantorovich duality result \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}mot\text{-}kantorovich\text{-}duality}\) equates the minimum with its finite dual. Applying the same result to the negative cost and multiplying both primal and dual values by \(-1\) proves the corresponding equality for the maximum. Hence both programs give exact convexified empirical endpoints.

It remains to prove the replication assertion, which is specific to this proposition. The constraints in (2) have rational coefficients and rational right-hand sides. A linear functional on a nonempty polytope has an optimal face containing an extreme point; every extreme point of this rational polytope is rational because its coordinates solve a full-rank subsystem of the active rational equalities. Thus a rational optimal plan exists. More generally, let \(\pi\) be any rational optimal plan. Put \(N=\sum_am_{nba}=n_{nb}\), and choose an integer \(L\) divisible by \(N\), by every \(m_{nba}\), and by every denominator occurring among the finitely many values \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\). Create
\[
L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}
\]
replicated units of joint type \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\). These multiplicities are nonnegative integers and sum to \(L\). By (2), the arm-\(a\) label \(i_a\) occurs exactly
\[
\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}}L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}
=\frac{L}{m_{nba}}
\tag{3}
\]
times. Therefore, within arm \(a\), every label is replicated by the integer factor \(L/m_{nba}\), and the empirical joint law on the replicated common unit labels is exactly \(\pi\). Set the replicated complete-randomization quota to \(m_{nba}'=(L/N)m_{nba}\); these are positive integers, preserve the original arm fractions, and sum to \(L\). Assigning to each replicated unit the corresponding centered armwise residual values, and choosing fixed potential outcomes and nodewise predictable fitted values whose difference equals those residuals, realizes the plan at that single history node. Repeating the construction at integer multiples of \(L\) gives nodewise completion attainability along growing replicated block sizes. The construction neither retains the original unreplicated block size nor enforces compatibility with any other history node, exactly as the proposition states.

As the smallest arithmetic stress test, take both centered lists to be \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\). For the unnormalized contrast \((1,-1)\), equal-rank pairing makes the squared contrast identically zero, while reverse-rank pairing makes it identically four. Hence the two costs are \(0\) and \(4\), and for a block of size four the associated envelope width is
\[
\frac{4w_{nb}^2}{4-1}>0.
\]
For the normalized contrast \((1,-1)/\sqrt2\), both costs and this width are divided by two. This verifies both the endpoint ordering and nontrivial width.

semantic_closure.name: \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\)
semantic_closure.construction: \[\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\left\{\Xi_n=\left((Y_{nbi}(a))_{b,i,a},(m_{nba}^{h})_{b,h,a},(g_{nbi}^{h}(a))_{b,h,i,a}\right):\begin{array}{l}(Y_{nbi}(a))_{b,i,a}\text{ is fixed before randomization};\\ (m_{nba}^{h})_{a\in\mathcal A}\text{ and }(g_{nbi}^{h}(a))_{i,a}\text{ are the evaluations of the same prespecified predictable allocation and fitting rules at every }h;\\ \text{for every }b\le B_n\text{ and }h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\ R_{nbi}^{h}(a)=Y_{nbi}(a)-g_{nbi}^{h}(a)\text{ has centered margins }\mu_{nba}^{h};\\ \gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\delta_{(R_{nbi}^{h}(1)-\bar R_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,R_{nbi}^{h}(K)-\bar R_{nbK}^{h})}\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\end{array}\right\}.\] Thus one member fixes common unit labels and all potential outcomes before assignment and induces the counts, fitted values, residual margins, feasible couplings, and transport endpoints at every node, including nodes off the realized path.

semantic_closure.name: \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n),\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n),U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)\)
semantic_closure.construction:
For \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), let \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\) be its nodewise conditional-variance contribution. With the predictable block weight already included in \(U_{nb}^{h}\) and \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\), define the normalized root-to-leaf compatibility gap
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}\ \sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}\frac1{s_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\left\{U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}-Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}\right\}.
\]
Define the single-node multi-index integrality diagnostic
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\sup_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}\left[\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma-J_{nb}^{h,-}\right].
\]
For a fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\), define the reduced nodewise contribution \(U_{nb}^{h,\rho}=(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h}\) and the corresponding root-to-leaf endpoint
\[
U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi),\rho}.
\]
The two gaps and \(U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)\) are retained only for the unresolved global history-tree compatibility problem; the fixed-fraction necessity result for uniform inference is certified separately by an explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass.

semantic_closure.name: Residual history-tree integer-flow handle
semantic_closure.construction: The fixed-fraction necessity direction for uniform inference is settled by the explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass in \(\text{thm:fixed-fraction-upper-endpoint-necessity}\). The remaining handle concerns only global adaptive-history compatibility: represent one ex ante sequence \((\Xi_n)_{n\ge1}\), with \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) and its entire induced triangular experiment-analysis array in \(\mathfrak D\), as a history-tree integer multi-index flow with common unit labels. Enforce prefix consistency by backward induction and compare its root-to-leaf objective with \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\). Use rational replication at an isolated node to measure \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), then characterize the additional loss caused by sharing one fixed potential-outcome array and one predictable fitting rule across incompatible branches while preserving membership in \(\mathfrak D\).

semantic_closure.name: \(\mathfrak D_M\)
semantic_closure.construction:
For a fixed \(M>0\), define the optional subclass
\[
\mathfrak D_M=\left\{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)):
\sup_{n\ge1}\max_{b\le B_n}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}
\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\max_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|\le M\right\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak D\); the displayed bound is an additional common history-uniform restriction and does not replace any member property of \(\mathfrak D\).

semantic_closure.name: Fixed-\(K\) empirical transportation program
semantic_closure.construction: Feed the observable measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)}\) from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\) into the finite program. When every \(m_{nba}>0\), optimize over variables \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\), indexed by \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\), the objective \[\sum_{i_1\in\mathcal O_{nb1}}\cdots\sum_{i_K\in\mathcal O_{nbK}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\left\{\sum_{a=1}^Kc_a\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)\right\}^2\] subject, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\), to the exact marginal constraints \[\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}.\] The minimum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and the maximum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\). If an arm sample is empty, represent its convention \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) by one artificial zero atom of mass one and solve the same marginal-coupling program; the admissible class never invokes this branch.

payload.tldr: Under predictable integer quotas followed by uniform complete randomization within each growing block, past-only AIPW adjustment yields a square-integrable martingale difference array. The paper derives the nodewise-exact predictable transport range and its pathwise sum inside the Cartesian convexified relaxation, without asserting one globally consistent adaptive-history completion. Observable assigned-arm residual margins estimate both endpoints uniformly at rate \(r_n=q_n^{-\kappa}\) over the common moment class and at rate \(q_n^{-1/2}\) over the bounded-residual endpoint class. Two-arm quantile sorting and a fixed-\(K\) finite transportation program compute the endpoints. Under the separately imposed predictable-QV stabilization condition, the estimated upper endpoint gives conservative unconditional martingale Wald coverage, while an explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass with \(V_n=U_n\) proves that every fixed fractional discount has a strict sub-nominal Gaussian coverage limit.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's adaptive design-based AIPW theory permits broad history-measurable block assignment laws and derives adaptive covariance and inference, but it does not characterize the residual-coupling range created by predictable fixed-count complete-block randomization. Static sharp-variance transport results do not supply a history-uniform observable endpoint rate or conservative studentization along an adaptive filtration.
project_justification.niche: Predictable quotas reduce every pre-block conditional variance to a finite-population coupling problem while leaving the accumulated predictable quadratic variation random. This permits nodewise transport optimization, history-uniform endpoint estimation, and martingale inference under a separately stated predictable-QV stabilization condition.
project_justification.fill: The contribution is the nodewise-exact rectangular predictable-QV envelope, exact two-arm sorting and fixed-\(K\) LP computation, the general moment-class rate \(q_n^{-\kappa}\), the bounded-residual rate \(q_n^{-1/2}\), conservative martingale Wald coverage from the observable upper endpoint, and a fixed-quota subclass certificate showing that no fixed fractional discount is uniformly valid. Cross-history realizability of independently selected nodewise plans is not claimed.

sampling_model.uniformity: The number of arms \(K\), overlap and moment constants, deterministic lower count sequence \(q_n\), leverage envelope \(\ell_n\), and QV lower constant \(v_0\) are common across \(\mathfrak D\). Conservative coverage is stated only on the further restricted class satisfying the separate uniform predictable-QV stabilization condition; that condition is not derived from the quota, overlap, count, leverage, moment, or QV-growth primitives.

payload.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026), Section 5, Definition 2, allow arbitrary history-measurable joint block assignment laws with positive unit-level marginals, and Theorem 6 gives block-adaptive finite-population AIPW covariance, normality, and conservative coverage. The predictable integer quotas and uniform complete-block draw used here are an explicit restriction of that framework. Their printed Supplementary Material, Lemma S4, is retained only as a mismatch receipt because its indicator uses an inverse variance threshold; the present martingale CLT is proved directly at the stated \(\epsilon\sigma_n\) threshold and invokes only the cited Lévy continuity criterion. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) formulate static multi-arm quadratic transport variance bounds, Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014) give the two-arm sorting prototype, Yu, Zhu, and Liu (2025) aggregate nonadaptive stratified bounds, and Mikhaeil and Green (2024) identify regression residuals as the coupling object for adjusted two-arm estimators. None supplies the present adaptive-history endpoint rates and studentization. Ober-Reynolds (2023) studies directional endpoint limits under iid empirical processes. Saco (2026) uses a different predictable-QV lower condition and realized-QV studentization. Harshaw, Middleton, and Savje (2026) optimize admissible quadratic bounds under arbitrary designs. Newby et al. (2025) provide a four-arm mental-health application target, but their participant-level contextual bandit is not the fixed-count complete-block design analyzed here; application requires a predictably batched redesign.
payload.technical_internal_limitation: The rectangular relaxation permits a separate convexified coupling at every possible history node. The exact-envelope theorem proves attainment at each node and, after independently selecting visited coordinates, attainment of the summed endpoints along a fixed path inside that Cartesian relaxation. It does not prove that one fixed potential-outcome array and one predictable fitting rule realize independently selected optimizers simultaneously across incompatible histories. No global completion class, compatibility-gap theorem, or cross-history sharpness claim is retained. The fixed-fraction no-discount certificate avoids this issue by using one explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass whose common-label coupling has zero contrast cost in every block.
payload.honest_scope: The delivered adaptive results are the nodewise-exact rectangular predictable complete-block transport envelope, observable history-uniform endpoint bounds over the general moment class and bounded-residual endpoint class, and conservative unconditional martingale Wald coverage under an additional uniform predictable-QV stabilization condition. Two-arm sorting, the fixed-\(K\) LP, and the two-block covariance enumeration support those results. The explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass establishes a genuine fixed-fraction no-discount certificate because \(V_n=U_n\) and \(\widehat U_n/U_n\to1\) there. Predictable quotas are a paper-specific design restriction, QV stabilization is a separate high-level assumption, and no theorem asserts cross-history realizability of independently optimized nodewise couplings. Static reductions and the \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\) enumeration are validation checks rather than additional contributions. The Newby et al. trial is a prospective consumer only after a predictably batched complete-block redesign.
